Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid

Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

def solve(inp):
    import collections
    bgc=collections.Counter(x for r in inp for x in r).most_common(1)[0][0]
    m=[(i,j) for i,r in enumerate(inp) for j,x in enumerate(r) if x!=bgc]
    h,w=len(inp),len(inp[0]); out=[row[:] for row in inp]
    cols={j for _,j in m}; rows={i for i,_ in m}
    # pair them into corner triplets: choose anchor as the marker forming right angle with both another row and col markers
    used=set()
    for a in m:
        if a in used: continue
        # find other markers sharing its row or column
        others=[b for b in m if b not in used and b!=a and (b[0]==a[0] or b[1]==a[1])]
        # need one same-row, one same-col
        sr=[b for b in others if b[0]==a[0]]
        sc=[b for b in others if b[1]==a[1]]
        if len(sr)>=1 and len(sc)>=1:
            # rectangle corners: TL=a, use sr min j as TR? demo had TL(0,4),TR(0,10),BR(10,10) - three points define rect; draw outline with color 2 unless that cell already marker
            c=2
            def put(i,j,v):
                if (i,j) in {(x,y,c_) for x,y,c_ in m}: out[i][j]=inp[i][j]
                else: out[i][j]=v
            for i in range(min(a[0],sr[0]),max(a[0],sr[0])+1):
                for j in [min(a[1],sc[0]),max(a[1],sc[0])]:
                    put(i,j,c)
            for j in range(min(a[1],sc[1]),max(a[1],sc[1])+1):
                for i in [min(a[0],sr[0]),max(a[0],sr[0])]:
                    put(i,j,c)
            used.add(a)
    return out

import collections
def analyze(k):
    t=G[k+' input']; o=G[k+' output']
    h,w=len(t),len(t[0])
    bgc=collections.Counter(x for r in t for x in r).most_common(1)[0][0]

    added=[(i,j) for i in range(h) for j in range(w) if t[i][j]==bgc and o[i][j]==2]
